title: SRE ops snapshot: incident triage and SLO trends (2026-06-27)
body:
Week: 2026-06-21 -> 2026-06-27
Owners: Priya Nambiar (author), Miguel Torres (outgoing oncall), Jonah Castillo (incoming)

Overview:
This snapshot captures the major SRE work this week: an intermittent 503/5xx incident affecting parts of the hosted API, a modest SLO burn for availability, follow-on mitigations and playbook gaps discovered during the oncall handoff. Notes below are intentionally granular — includes timeline, temporary mitigations, and concrete follow-ups (owners + rough ETA).

1) Incident summary — KV cache corruption (hosted-api ded-3 pool)
- Incident window: 2026-06-23 02:14 UTC -> 2026-06-23 08:40 UTC (primary impact); recurring spikes 2026-06-25 01:40 UTC -> short bursts of errors until mitigated
- Symptoms: 503s and 502s on text-generation endpoints for customers routed to ded-3; elevated error rates and client retries that amplified tail latency.
- Detection: automated SLO alert on error-rate (alerts/sre/error-rate/hosted-api-availability) at 02:18 UTC. Pager routed to primary oncall (Miguel). Incident channel: #incident-ded3 (see linked_confluence runbook).
- Immediate mitigation timeline:
  * 02:20: Applied temporary routing rule to divert 20% of traffic from ded-3 to ded-2 (manual rollback safe test)
  * 02:38: Observed partial recovery in error-rate for diverted traffic; errors persisted on ded-3 pool
  * 03:05: Drained affected worker nodes in ded-3 and restarted runtime processes (control-plane drain + rolling restart); KV cache rebuild started
  * 04:30: Error-rate decreased below alert threshold for most tenants; full recovery by 08:40 after background cache rebuild completed for long-lived sessions
- Impact: approx 0.03% weekly availability SLO burn for hosted-api; several high-volume tenants saw increased latency and retries leading to higher token cost. No data loss reported.

Root cause (initial RCA):
- A runtime regression introduced in runtime PR#782 caused an edge-case in continuous-batching when sequences > 1024 tokens were routed to a worker with a half-populated KV cache. Under this condition a stale pointer led to occasional memory corruption of the cache structure; that in turn caused runtime to fail fast and return 5xx for in-flight requests.
- Contributing factors:
  * No unit test covering >1024 sequence lengths combined with cached prefix conditions
  * Runbook lacked a straightforward diagnostic to confirm KV-cache integrity (operators were forced to do process-level inspection)

Work done / changes merged this week:
- Reverted the risky kernel selection patch in runtime PR#782 (hotfix revert merged: runtime PR#785) — deployed to ded pools with canary first.
- Short-term routing rule added to reduce blast radius until new tests land.
- Added increased sampling for slow requests (instrumentation) to help debug future cache-corruption signals.

2) SLO health snapshot (weekly)
- Availability SLO (hosted-api): target 99.95%
  * Observed (this week): 99.92% -> error budget burn ~30%
- Latency SLOs (all endpoints combined):
  * P50: 28ms (stable)
  * P95: 210ms (up from 150ms baseline due to retries and few cold cache events)
  * P99: 1.4s (tail impacted by the incident and retries)
- Key takeaway: the incident was the primary driver of SLO erosion; without it we'd be within target. Need to harden cache correctness and reduce retry amplification.

3) Oncall handoff notes (Miguel -> Jonah)
- Outgoing summary from Miguel:
  * Primary incident described above — mitigation steps documented in incident channel, temporary routing rule remains in place until runtime tests land.
  * Night coverage note: monitor ded-3 error-rate and P99 latency during the 00:00–06:00 UTC window (history shows more noisy replays overnight).
  * Watch for autoscaler flapping on ded-2 after we diverted 20% of traffic (some odd interactions between scaling cooldown and routing weight changes).
- Handoff checklist completed: playbooks reviewed, active alerts annotated, oncall escalation roster confirmed.

4) Playbook and process gaps discovered
- Runbook gap: lack of a quick diagnostic to check KV cache integrity (no single command returns cache health).
- Testing gap: no regression test for combined path (continuous-batching + prefix caching + long sequences).
- Observability gap: insufficient sampling of internal runtime errors (most were swallowed and only surfaced as 5xx at the API layer).

5) Action items (owners + ETA)
- Add unit/integration test covering >1024 token sequences + prefix cache scenarios — Owner: Asha Patel — ETA: 2026-07-04
- Implement a "kv-cache health" diagnostic endpoint (read-only) and add to runbook — Owner: Jonah Castillo — ETA: 2026-07-08
- Create alert that watches for rapid increase in duplicate client retries on the same session (reduces amplification) — Owner: Kira Singh — ETA: 2026-07-01
- Harden canary deployment: automated canary for runtime changes that exercises long-sequence paths — Owner: Priya Nambiar (me) — ETA: 2026-07-11
- Postmortem doc (inc. timeline + RCA + remediation verification plan) — Owner: Miguel Torres — ETA: 2026-06-30 (draft)

6) Capacity & recent infra churn
- Notable: ded-3 had a node replacement on 2026-06-16 which introduced slightly different kernel versions on a handful of nodes (investigating whether mismatch increased vulnerability to the PR#782 regression).
- Action: infra to run node kernel homogeneity check across dedicated pools — Owner: infra-team (linked ticket: JIRA-4399) — ETA: 2026-07-05

7) Misc: smaller items and notes
- Observability: Added a temporary dashboard tile for "kv-cache errors by pool" in Redwood Console (temporary until new metrics are emitted).
- Training: schedule a 30-min lunch-and-learn for oncall to walk through the new diagnostic endpoint (when implemented).
- Customer comms: CS notified top affected tenants; no emergency SLA credits issued but we have a comms draft if escalations come in (see linked_artifacts).

8) Risks / ask for leadership
- Request temporary freeze on further kernel-level runtime experiments until canary path validated; need product/infrastructure alignment.
- Request additional SRE headcount hours next 2 weeks to expedite tests and runbook improvements (covered in separate staffing request thread).

9) Next steps for next week's snapshot
- Confirm postmortem published and remediation verified in staging.
- Confirm kv-cache health endpoint appears in staging and is exercised by automated tests.
- Re-evaluate SLO burn after the postmortem actions (target to return to <= 10% weekly error budget burn by 2026-07-11).

Appendix (quick links & commands) — kept brief here, full runbook on Confluence:
- Incident channel: #incident-ded3 (Slack)
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SRE-Runbooks/kv-cache-corruption
- Diagnostic hint: "ps aux | grep runtime" + "curl -s http://<node>:9100/kv-cache-health" (placeholder until endpoint exists)

Prepared by: Priya Nambiar (eng-sre)
Reviewed by: Miguel Torres, Asha Patel

End of snapshot.
